(a) In General.—Section 2430 of title 10, United States Code, is amended in subsection (a)—
        (1) by redesignating paragraphs (1) and (2) as subparagraphs (A) and (B), respectively; 
        (2) by striking “In this chapter” and inserting “(1) Except as provided under paragraph (2), in this chapter”; and 
        (3) by adding at the end the following new paragraph:“(2) In this chapter, the term ‘major defense acquisition program’ does not include an acquisition program or project that is carried out using the rapid fielding or rapid prototyping acquisition pathway under section 804 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2016 (Public Law 114–92; 10 U.S.C. 2302 note).”.  
    (b) Annual Reporting.—The Secretary of Defense shall include in each comprehensive annual Selected Acquisition Report submitted under section 2432 of title 10, United States Code, a listing of all programs or projects being developed or procured under the exceptions to the definition of major defense acquisition program set forth in paragraph (2) of section 2430(a) of United States Code, as added by subsection (a)(1)(C) of this section.

fable.w: The section amends the definition of 'major defense acquisition program' and requires the Secretary of Defense to list excepted programs in the annual Selected Acquisition Report, which goes to Congress. The reporting requirement may look like a participation procedure, but Congress is inside the federal government, so no outside party is consulted or given a role in any federal decision. There is no rulemaking, public comment, advisory body, or right to sue.
fable.s: The Secretary of Defense shall include in each comprehensive annual Selected Acquisition Report submitted under section 2432 of title 10, United States Code, a listing of all programs or projects

qwen_block.w: This section requires the Secretary of Defense to submit a report to Congress (implied by the reference to the Selected Acquisition Report submitted under section 2432). Reporting to Congress is an internal government action, as Congress is part of the federal government. There is no requirement for consultation with or participation by outside parties such as the public, states, or private entities.
qwen_block.s: The Secretary of Defense shall include in each comprehensive annual Selected Acquisition Report submitted under section 2432 of title 10, United States Code, a listing of all programs or projects being developed or procured under the exceptions to the definition of major defense acquisition program set forth in paragraph (2) of section 2430(a) of United States Code, as added by subsection (a)(1)(C) of this section.

opus.w: The section narrows the definition of 'major defense acquisition program' and requires the Secretary of Defense to list the excluded programs in the Selected Acquisition Reports sent to Congress. Reporting to Congress stays inside the federal government, so it is not participation. No outside party is consulted, given a hearing or comment period, placed on an advisory body or given a right to sue over a federal decision. The procedural feel of the reporting requirement is a trap.
opus.s: The Secretary of Defense shall include in each comprehensive annual Selected Acquisition Report submitted under section 2432 of title 10, United States Code, a listing of all programs or projects being developed or procured under the exceptions to the definition of major defense acquisition program
opus.b: Step 1 (the tempting reading): The "Annual Reporting" subsection looks procedural, because it makes the Secretary of Defense list certain programs in each Selected Acquisition Report. But those reports go to Congress under 10 U.S.C. 2432, and Congress is inside the federal government. Subsection (a) only changes a definition. No one outside the government (states, industry, experts or the public) is consulted, holds a hearing, sits on an advisory body, comments on a rule or gets a right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends definitions and requires the Secretary of Defense to include specific information in an annual report. The definition of participation excludes reports to Congress or other federal agencies, as these are internal government communications. There is no requirement to consult with states, tribes, the public, or other non-federal entities before making a decision. The 'Selected Acquisition Report' is an internal government document.
qwen_chat.s: (b) Annual Reporting.—The Secretary of Defense shall include in each comprehensive annual Selected Acquisition Report submitted under section 2432 of title 10, United States Code, a listing of all programs or projects being developed or procured under the exceptions to the definition of major defense acquisition program set forth in paragraph (2) of section 2430(a) of United States Code, as added by subsection (a)(1)(C) of this section.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "Annual Reporting" requirement involves participation because it requires the Secretary of Defense to submit a report. However, the definition explicitly states that reports to Congress or other federal entities are inside the government and do not constitute participation. Furthermore, the text does not specify that the report goes to Congress (though it likely does under the referenced statute), but even if it did, it is an internal government reporting requirement, not a consultation with outsiders. The rest of the section is purely definitional and procedural regarding internal military acquisition pathways.
